scenario.title: BATTLE OF LAKE KHASAN - 2 AUG 1938
intro.text:
BATTLE OF LAKE KHASAN - 2 AUG 1938

Lake Khasan, Far East of Soviet Union

The sneaky Japanese attacked and beaten our border troops on the Bezymyannaya and Zaozyornaya hills. Attack the Japanese with superior power and recapture the territories we deserve!

ORDERS
After 9 turns control 7/6/5 VH for a BV/V/TV.

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank (+1)
2x Infantry (+2)
1x Reconnaissance
1x Artillery (+1)
header.act: ACT I — LESSONS BEFORE THE GREAT WAR
header.location: Lake Khasan, Soviet Far East — 2 August 1938
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.reaction-briliant.text: Illescas fell quickly. Moscow wants the photographs; Volkov wants to know how the companies got so far apart. I've sent both.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.reaction-victory.text: The towns south of Madrid were taken, but neither armour nor infantry can claim it acted alone. That has not stopped both camps from trying.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.reaction-tactical.text: We lost tanks in Spain and wore the infantry out keeping up with them. I've been asked which arm let the other down. I'd rather speak to the crews first.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-a.text: The tank officers keep quoting your Illescas order at me. They expect to go straight through again. Have they seen the ground here?
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: I'm keeping the Spain march tables. We did get the guns and infantry to the same place, whatever Pavel says about the time it took.
line.scene-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-0.text: I found the photograph from Spain in the transport file. Two faces have been cut out, neatly enough that the scissors took part of Antonov's sleeve.
line.scene-1.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.scene-1.text: Put it away, Anna. Not here. We've been told which names may go into the reports.
line.scene-2.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-2.text: The engineers' stakes are sinking. I can't recommend an approach until they've walked it again, and the Japanese guns can see most of the marsh.
line.decision.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.decision.text: We have orders to recover the border heights. Do we attack both now, or give the engineers and batteries time to prepare? They can improve the approaches; they can't conceal the preparations.
line.decision.choice.mass-the-assault.te: Mass the striking force and keep pressure on both heights without pause.
line.decision.choice.mass-the-assault.hi: Give infantry 18 experience and artillery 12 experience, and gain 50 prestige for accepting the immediate assault timetable.
Let engineers mark firm approaches and artillery register before the infantry moves.
Attach an experienced eight-strength 1936 engineer detachment; the special transport and equipment cost 60 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-a-0.text: I'll send the reserves toward whichever slope makes progress. They'll have to follow before we can sort out every report.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-a-1.text: Give the casualty clerks the rolls before the attack. All the names, Anna. They must be able to find a missing man afterward.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-b-0.text: Then the infantry waits. Tell the batteries why; I don't want a gunner mistaking movement in those lanes for the first wave.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-b-1.text: And if a patrol finds a lane unusable, the battalion stops. Will you back me when headquarters asks why it hasn't moved?
line.post-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.post-0.text: I'll keep the photograph in the transport file. Now, I need the engineers' latest report. Has anyone brought it in?
